children: A number of stocks jumped in the afternoon session after an AI and chip sell-off pushed the S&P 500 into correction territory and drove traders into defensive shares. Tech selling deepened as Anthropic fell more than 10% a day after its Nasdaq debut while Nvidia slid over 7% and AMD dropped 11%, leaving the Nasdaq down more than 3%, CNBC data showed. Fed Governor Lisa Cook warned in remarks covered by CNBC against delaying rate hikes.

Steady grocery demand from the previous session reinforced the bid after Walmart's earnings results showed Q3 revenue up 5.2% to $188.8 billion and a raised outlook, with CFO John David Rainey citing mid-single-digit U.S. grocery growth on the call.

When growth valuations compress alongside rate-hike fears, capital rotates to household and grocery names with steadier cash flows. Packaged food's lead over big-box retailers suggests investors are favoring cheaper defensives with room to rebound rather than paying up for crowded retail leaders.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

children: Zooming in on Edgewell Personal Care

Edgewell Personal Care’s shares are quite volatile and have had 17 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

Edgewell Personal Care is up 70.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $28.71 per share, it is trading close to its 52-week high of $29.66 from November 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Edgewell Personal Care’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $641.42.
